text:
Gabriel Landeskog won the Masterton and the Mark Messier Leadership Award for last season's return, and this year he's past the comeback story and into a big role. With Nathan MacKinnon out, his minutes have crept up to around 17 a night, and he has nine goals and 15 points in 24 games.

The goals are running hot: nine on 7.2 expected, a 27% shooting rate that no forward keeps. But the rest of his on-ice luck has gone the other way. Colorado has scored about five fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, which has cost him assists, and the Avalanche take about 59% of expected goals at five on five when he's out there. Those two should even out over time.

He also showed the edge he plays with on Wednesday: a power-play goal in a win over Montreal, a hit that sent Kaiden Guhle out injured (per Sportsnet), and pointed words for the Xhekaj brothers' late-game antics, as the Denver Post's Corey Masisak reported. What to watch: whether the chances keep coming without MacKinnon.
headline: Landeskog's comeback has teeth
